thread_a.role: TCP sendmsg advances write_seq (under socket lock)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(write_seq)]) from thread_b (the lockless readiness read must not be torn by a concurrent send-side write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the send-side write holds the socket lock, but tcp_stream_memory_free runs from the poll/readiness path (and IRQ/other CPUs) without the socket lock; the two accesses share no lock, so no serialize(g) establishes the single-access atomicity the reader assumes
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write to the sequence field -> data race (store-tearing / torn read)

fix_maps_to: patch wraps the write_seq writes in WRITE_ONCE and the lockless reads in READ_ONCE -> makes the conflicting single access atomic; a tearing annotation, not a serialize/order/counts guarantee
recall_risk_notes: Same shape as the snd_nxt case: object and sites are in the static surface and the category maps to atomic(single access)=data_race, but tcp_stream_memory_free is a best-effort readiness check (notsent_bytes = write_seq - snd_nxt) that tolerates a stale snapshot. The read carries no order intent beyond no-tearing and there is no semantic guard, so the LLM is likely to adjudicate it benign and reject (precision pressure); only a pure-syntactic-race detector would fire. The fix is annotation-only and does not map onto serialize/order/counts.
